cues: Arrhenius is the narrowest, tied to water.
Lewis is the widest, but it is so wide that it says nothing about the relative strengths of acids, and it even struggles to call hydrochloric acid an acid in the strict sense.
text: Compare the three. Arrhenius is the narrowest, tied to water. Bronsted and Lowry is wider. Lewis is the widest, but it is so wide that it says nothing about the relative strengths of acids, and it even struggles to call hydrochloric acid an acid in the strict sense.
